# Fairpractice Review Replies (`fairpractice-review-replies`)

Checks draft replies to online reviews for what gets practices fined: words that confirm the reviewer was a patient (your visit, your treatment, our records show), health details, the reviewer's name and visit dates or times, lists low-rated reviews with no reply, and writes safe generic reply drafts a person approves. Reviewer names are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairpractice Review Replies never posts to Google, Yelp or any review site. Fairpractice Review Replies never contacts a reviewer.**

Fairpractice ver 1 · Compliance pack · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairpractice-core`](../fairpractice-core)

```bash
npx -y fairpractice-review-replies demo
npx -y fairpractice-review-replies mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: Bluewater Family Medicine (a made-up practice) and made-up reviewers. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`reviews.csv`](fixtures/reviews.csv): Planted: a safe reply to a 5-star review (G-101); a reply that uses the reviewer's name, a weekday and "your visit", "our records show" and "your lab" (G-102); a reply that says "your bill" (G-103); a 1-star review with no reply (G-104); a reply that repeats the reviewer's own health detail (Y-105); and a safe reply (G-106).
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): the practice name and office phone that safe replies use. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `reviews_check` | List draft replies that confirm a patient relationship or give health details, and low-rated reviews with no reply. | runs |
| `reviews_write_report` | Write reviews.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and reviews.html into out_dir (default fairpractice-out/reviews). | runs |
| `reviews_draft_review_reply` | Write a short reply for one review that never confirms the reviewer was a patient and moves complaints offline. | asks first |
| `reviews_request_post` | After one named human click (even in Auto), record that the reviewed review reply draft is approved in review_reply-requests.csv. | asks first |
| `reviews_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `reviews_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `reviews_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `reviews_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `review_reply_publish` | Fairpractice Review Replies never posts to Google, Yelp or any review site. | refused |
| `reviewer_contact` | Fairpractice Review Replies never contacts a reviewer. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `reviews_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `reviews` (required) | Reviews export under --root: review id, platform, reviewer, rating, review text and your draft reply |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: practice_name, contact_phone, low_rating, extra_phrases, extra_words |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairpractice-review-replies inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Reviews and draft replies (`reviews`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `review_id` | text | Review ID, Review #, ID, Review |
| `platform` | text | Platform, Site, Source, Channel |
| `reviewer` | text (masked) | Reviewer, Reviewer Name, Author, Name, Posted By |
| `rating` | number | Rating, Stars, Score |
| `review` | text | Review Text, Text, Comment, Body, Content |
| `reply` | text | Reply, Draft Reply, Response, Our Reply, Proposed Reply |

## Settings file (`reviews_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `practice_name` | Name to sign replies with |
| `contact_phone` | Office manager phone (or email) to move complaints offline |
| `low_rating` | Ratings at or below this need a reply; default 2 |
| `extra_phrases` | More phrases that confirm a visit in your specialty |
| `extra_words` | More health words to flag |

## Memory

`reviews_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `reviews_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairpractice-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairpractice-review-replies": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairpractice-review-replies",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairpractice-review-replies -- npx -y fairpractice-review-replies mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairpractice-review-replies tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairpractice-review-replies sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairpractice-review-replies inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairpractice-review-replies call reviews_check '{"reviews":"<reviews>"}'
fairpractice-review-replies eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairpractice-review-replies demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
